title: Elizabeth Warren Targets Trump, Big Tech Over 'Massive Tax Breaks' for AI and Data Centers
key_facts: Sen. Elizabeth Warren said in an X post and video on Saturday 3 Oct 2026 that Meta, Amazon, Alphabet and Microsoft are spending billions on AI and data centers while receiving 'massive tax breaks' from Trump and Republicans.

She said the issue has been 'totally under the radar', that the size of the deductions and the lobbying behind them are unknown, and that she is pressing Mark Zuckerberg and other executives for answers.
She linked the breaks to budget cuts: 'Republicans are filling the hole in our budget by slashing health care for millions of Americans.'
Benzinga adds that Meta reportedly classified some AI data centers as 'pilot models' to claim federal tax credits, cutting its 2025 tax bill by $3.9 billion.

Context: Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker urged lawmakers to reject AI and Big Tech influence; Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz proposed a tax on large social platforms; Sen. Bernie Sanders proposed that major AI companies put 50% of their stock in a sovereign wealth fund.
Rep. Ro Khanna criticised the voluntary White House AI agreement, which Zuckerberg reportedly helped shape, for lacking penalties and oversight.
quote_evidence: "People across the country are worried about AI, cyberattacks, and job loss," she said.
"We don't know the magnitude of these tax out. We don't know what lobbying the companies did to obtain these tax out," she said.
Meta also reportedly classified some AI data centers as "pilot models" to claim federal tax credits, reducing its 2025 tax bill by $3.9 billion.
why_it_matters_hint: A senior Democratic senator opens a line of attack on the tax side of the AI buildout and demands disclosure from the four biggest spenders.
notes: TradingView carries Benzinga's text; Benzinga is the source. Benzinga says the piece was partly produced with AI tools and reviewed by its editors. The $3.9 billion Meta figure is 'reportedly', unattributed in the text. Benzinga's own URL not shown; url is the TradingView page.
